newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Interpump to debut on bourse mid Dec. [CORRECTED 18:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Italy's Interpump to debut on bourse mid Dec. [CORRECTED 18:30 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects date of debut in headline from Dec 16)

Italian company Interpump, which makes high-pressure piston pumps and cleaning machines, intends to make its debut on the Milan stock market in the week of December 16, (corrects) the global coordinator for its private placement said.
Claudio Costamagna of global coordinator Goldman Sachs said the offer price, between 5,700 and 6,700 lire, will be published on December 4, the day before the public sale offer opens.
Interpump is currently 80 percent owned by private group BC Partners, with the rest owned by Banca Commerciale Italiana, management and private investors.
The offering will be the 14th entry on the Milan stock market this year.
Interpump had sales of 224 billion lire in the first six months of this year with an operating result of 40 billion and gross operating margin of 18 percent.

It forecasts sales and gross operating margins for the whole year will match 1995 levels of 395 billion and 17 percent while net profit would be impacted by financial charges estimated at 12 billion, its prospectus said.
It said net profit should be slightly higher than the 10.17 billion seen in the first half of 1996.

Based on a mid-range price, proceeds from the placement were estimated at 130 billion lire and would be used partly to reduce debt, to repay a loan from the shareholders and to go into reserves, managing director Giovanni Cavallini said.
Net financial debt at the end of 1996 was expected to be around 70 billion from 187 billion in June 1996.
Some 25.8 million shares will go on the market, or 32 percent of capital, of which 20 million will derive from a capital increase.
The company planned a so-called "greenshoe" over-allotment option of a further 15 percent.
